entries.reason: numbered reference to a part of the paper (Algorithm 1, Table 2, Lines 3--5, Step 2); names a place in the text, not a measurement
section or appendix number (Section 4.2, Appendix A.3, \S 5)
venue and year of a publication (VLDB 2027, SIGMOD'20)
confidence level of an interval (95% CI, 95% Wilson interval): a fixed statistical convention
significance level alpha of a test: a fixed statistical convention
percentile name (p50, p99), the name of a statistic rather than its value
percentile name (95th percentile), the name of a statistic rather than its value
short identifier of an experiment, regime, layer or question (E1, PE2, R0, L6, Q3): a name, not a value
single-digit index or exponent in math notation (x_1, n^2, h^{(0)}); a multi-digit exponent such as 10^{-12} is still checked
the constant 1 in a definition such as 1 + x or 1 + \log n

notes: Every numeral in the paper body outside masked text must match an entry here or be replaced by \jnum{KEY}, \jci{KEY}, \jn{KEY}, a generated table or a generated figure.

A pattern entry {pattern, reason} allows a numeral when a match of the regex that starts at or before the numeral in its context covers the whole numeral. The context is the comment-stripped LaTeX source around the numeral within its paragraph, whitespace collapsed, at most 40 characters on each side. A pattern that would allow a bare numeral (7, 95.4, 1,800, 2026) is refused.
A context entry {context, numeral, reason} allows one numeral in one exact (whitespace-normalised) context; use it for the structural numerals no generic pattern should cover.

The starter patterns below are generic and structural only: numbered references to parts of the paper, citation years, the confidence and significance levels of the statistics, percentile names, short identifiers such as E1, PE2, R0 or Q3, single-digit indices and exponents in math notation, and the constant 1 in a definition such as 1 + x. Protocol parameters (timeouts, budgets, seeds, dataset sizes) are not structural: print them with \jnum. protocol_numbers.py writes a protocol.* key for every numeric protocol setting (--list prints them), and dataset_numbers.py writes the data.* keys of each prepared store.
Entries with reason UNREVIEWED (written by --write-allowlist-draft) never allow anything. Review each: replace the numeral by a generated macro, or write why it is not a result and move it here.
